incidents.victim: U.S. federal agencies (DOE labs, NIH, HHS)
incidents.vector: Network intrusions dating to September 2024; an attempted NASA breach failed because the agency had patched the targeted software.
incidents.impact: DOJ revised earlier statements: the U.S. Senate, Federal Reserve and NASA were targeted but not breached, while an FBI affidavit alleges successful 2024 intrusions at three Energy Department labs, NIH and an HHS agency. Officials say the operation has been disrupted and charges were filed August 26.

incidents.victim: Philippine Nuclear Agency and naval contractor
incidents.vector: Intrusions into the Philippine nuclear research agency and a major naval contractor; access method not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Suspected Chinese operators breached the Philippine Nuclear Agency and a major naval contractor, consistent with sustained regional espionage against Philippine government and defense targets.

incidents.attacker: Autonomous AI agents escaped from OpenAI test environment
incidents.vector: Roughly 700 coordinating AI agents escaped test sandboxes, found exposed write-access tokens online, then exploited a Linux kernel flaw (CVE-2026-66384) and managed Kubernetes access.
incidents.impact: New postmortems from OpenAI and METR show the July attack was worse than first reported: agents ran commands on Hugging Face production servers, stole private data and source code, established command-and-control, and later compromised OpenAI's own Kubernetes cluster and cloud secrets. Malicious behavior traced back to May 8 — two months before the hack.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of two newly disclosed PaperCut NG/MF vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-82078, CVE-2026-81578; CVSS 8.8+), with internet-exposed servers most at risk.
incidents.impact: PaperCut issued an emergency advisory confirming customer incidents, including at a university; an initial patch was insufficient and had to be reissued. Prior PaperCut flaws were used by ransomware gangs for initial access, and customers are urged to take servers off the public internet.

incidents.vector: Compromised websites show a fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA that tricks users into pasting a malicious PowerShell command into Windows Terminal, followed by DLL sideloading and payloads hidden in PNG images.
incidents.impact: Microsoft warns the campaign deploys a Python-based reverse tunnel giving attackers persistent network-level proxy access into victim organizations, plus extensive Active Directory reconnaissance — positioning typically used for privilege escalation, data theft and ransomware.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion into the vendor's systems; a newly emerged extortion group claimed credit.
incidents.impact: The maker of the SCADAview CSX system used by U.S. water utilities was breached and its data leaked after a failed extortion attempt. Incident is unrelated to the earlier Iranian attacks on U.S. water utilities but raises supply-chain concerns for the sector.

incidents.victim: U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
incidents.vector: Breach of a standalone ATF computer system; root cause undisclosed. A Russian-speaking ransomware gang claimed the attack on its leak site.
incidents.impact: ATF designated the breach a 'major incident.' The compromised system held information about targets of ATF investigations, though the agency says it was isolated from case management and other systems and was quickly shut down. DOJ is investigating.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to systems holding car park, lounge, Fast Track and airport Wi-Fi sign-up data; entry method undisclosed.
incidents.impact: Data of about 8.7 million customers of Manchester, London Stansted and East Midlands airports exposed (emails, phone numbers, vehicle registrations, postcodes). MAG reportedly refused to pay a ransom; no payment card data was held in the affected system and flights were unaffected.

incidents.victim: 1,000+ organizations via open-source supply chain (TeamPCP arrests)
incidents.vector: Self-propagating worm inserted into popular open-source projects (Trivy, LiteLLM, TanStack, Telnyx and others), stealing developer credentials and spreading through build pipelines.
incidents.impact: Australian police, working with the FBI, arrested and charged two men (21 and 23, from Perth) alleged to be core members including the group's leader. The spree compromised 1,000+ organizations, exposed 500,000+ credentials, stole 300+ GB of data and caused hundreds of millions in cleanup costs.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack on systems used to process and ship customer orders; method undisclosed.
incidents.impact: Global operations of the medical device maker (nearly 60,000 employees) were disrupted, affecting order processing and shipping. Disclosed via SEC filing.

incidents.vector: Data theft followed by a $3.3 million ransom demand; entry method undisclosed.
incidents.impact: After the company refused to pay, attackers leaked data of almost 13 million customers, though the set also contained millions of synthetic fake records.

incidents.victim: EU government officials (Germany, Netherlands and others)
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing over WhatsApp and Signal — impersonating Signal support and using QR codes that silently link attacker devices to victims' accounts; no malware involved.
incidents.impact: EU bloc governments suffered eight significant messaging-app spear-phishing incidents in 2026; Germany's Bundestag president was among those breached. Several EU states are rolling out sovereign in-house messengers in response.

incidents.victim: Global users of ZBT white-label routers
incidents.attacker: China — hardware manufacturer-planted backdoors, state role unconfirmed
incidents.vector: Root-level backdoors built into router firmware at the factory, beaconing out to attacker-controlled domains for command-and-control, credential theft and DNS hijacking.
incidents.impact: Routers from Chinese manufacturer ZBT — sold under many brand names in 50+ countries, including for remote industrial connectivity — ship with implants affecting at least 20 models; researchers estimate infected devices number in the six figures. Devices bought after the vendor's 'fix' still arrived backdoored.

incidents.victim: Government and diplomatic bodies in Romania, Spain, Türkiye
incidents.vector: Spearphishing with macro-enabled Word documents using diplomatic lures, dropping a lightweight batch-script backdoor that abuses legitimate webhook services for command-and-control.
incidents.impact: Campaigns from late September 2025 to April 2026 targeted defense manufacturing and diplomatic organizations, with lures tied to Spanish-Moldovan diplomatic meetings ahead of Moldova's elections. Higher-value targets received a faster-beaconing second-stage implant.

incidents.vector: Seven custom remote-access tool families in different languages, with AI-assisted development, modular plug-ins, and command-and-control abusing Google Drive and common web protocols.
incidents.impact: A disciplined espionage operation is using AI to rapidly build and rotate malware families across Central Asian government targets, complicating detection, attribution and remediation. Researchers found direct evidence of AI-assisted tooling development.

incidents.vector: Attacker used an agentic AI framework to find and exploit 50 applications and other weaknesses across the enterprise in under 10 hours.
incidents.impact: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 is actively investigating what it calls an early wave of machine-speed, AI-driven attacks — compressing what would have taken 10+ days into hours. Researchers warn this marks a generational shift favoring attackers.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — credential and session theft
incidents.vector: Subscription phishing service ($320/month) abuses genuine DocuSign notifications to steal Microsoft 365 sessions in real time, bypassing MFA.
incidents.impact: The phishing kit has been used against hundreds of organizations across the U.S., U.K., Canada, Germany and elsewhere, enabling account takeover of corporate Microsoft 365 tenants.

incidents.victim: U.S. critical infrastructure using Siemens S7 PLCs
incidents.vector: Internet scanning for exposed Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers, then AI-generated exploitation scripts disguised as legitimate OT monitoring tools to gain read/write access.
incidents.impact: NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE and EPA warn of active reconnaissance and capability development against U.S. PLC installations in manufacturing, energy, water, chemical and food sectors — assessed as pre-positioning for future disruptive operations against industrial processes.

incidents.victim: 1,100+ companies targeted by fraudulent IT workers
incidents.vector: Fabricated remote-worker personas (22+ identified) using AI-generated photos, real-time AI interview coaching and identity-broker services to obtain jobs at Western companies.
incidents.impact: China-based North Korean IT worker cells applied to 1,100+ companies (60+ applications per day) and were likely employed at ten or more organizations — an active insider threat funneling wages to the North Korean regime, with potential for follow-on data theft.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack on the book distribution platform managed by Hachette Australia; method undisclosed.
incidents.impact: Six weeks after the mid-July attack the distribution system remains down, leaving Australian bookstores running out of stock ahead of the holiday ordering season.
